extracted.intended_audience: extramural grants administrative staff (Signing Officials, Principal Investigators, program directors, delegates) using eRA Commons
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance and policy rules in eRA Commons for closeout tasks (FFR, Final RPPR, Final Invention Statement, FRAM), trainee reporting tools (xTRACT/xTrain), administrative supplements, and Change of Institution/relinquishing statements including roles, validation, and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: TPPR multiple submissions / prior-submission view
rubrics_metrics.description: As long as the TPPR is not yet accepted, you can continue to upload and submit the TPPR as many times as needed. Each submission replaces the prior submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission a View Prior Submission button becomes available on Closeout Status to see the entire submission as a PDF with application information, who uploaded it and when, followed by the uploaded file's contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FFR) required for closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Financial Report (FFR) is required for closeout and should be prepared according to instructions provided by the awarding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commons users with the FSR role see the Manage Final FFR action on Closeout Status. For DHHS-funded awards, initiation may occur in eRA Commons but users are redirected to the Payment Management System (PMS) to fill out/submit the report; users need appropriate PMS access. For DOC-funded awards, the FFR is initiated and filled within eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission authority for closeout reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a signing official (SO) or a user with delegated report submit authority can submit the reports or other data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program director/principal investigator (PD/PI) can upload, preview, delete and save the closeout report submission package but cannot complete the final step to submit. This rule is repeated for FFR, Final RPPR, Final Invention Statement, FRAM, and other closeout actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR applicability and form restrictions (non-NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with the awarding agency for policy guidance on Final Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs). The F. Changes form and the H. Budget form are not applicable for Final RPPRs; the I. Outcomes form is applicable only for Final RPPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit a Final RPPR: log into eRA Commons as the contact PD/PI, access Closeout Status, click Process Final RPPR (PI can initiate; only SO can submit), edit the RPPR forms and submit. See Editing the RPPR Forms for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement (FIS) timing requirement (NIH/AHRQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: For NIH and AHRQ-funded awards you must submit a Final Invention Statement (FIS) within 120 days following the termination of a grant award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should include all inventions conceived or first reduced to practice during the course of work under the grant from the original effective date through completion/termination. Refer to the Procedure for Submission of Final Invention Statement and Certification for policy details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement: how to add and submit inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: To add an invention: type Name of Inventor, Title of Invention, and Date Reported to DHSS, then click Add Invention and Save. Use Confirm Invention popup and click Agree and Continue (even if more inventions to add). When all inventions are listed click Submit (only SO sees Submit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any inventions defined are saved immediately. While not yet submitted, a PI or SO can delete an item using Delete Invention and Save. Click Preview to download a PDF copy of the filled form. On submission, the submitted PDF is available via View on Closeout Status; Confirm/Agree popups appear during steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Invention Statement: reporting no inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: To certify that no inventions exist: click Save with No Inventions, confirm that Preview button changes to Preview (No Inventions Reported), then click Submit (only SO sees Submit) and agree to the certification popup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A success message appears; the submitted PDF (No Inventions Reported) is available on Closeout Status via View. Only SO can submit the no-inventions certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM purpose and initiation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM) lets recipients enter, review, route, and submit information in response to program official (PO) requests for additional information related to the Final RPPR. Either the PD/PI or SO can initiate the FRAM and attach a file or type/paste a Revised Project Outcomes, but only an SO can submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A FRAM task appears on Closeout Status when a PO requests additional materials. PD/PI receives email with description of requested material. Agency-specific guidance and tips appear on the FRAM screen; read that language carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM screen sections and what to submit where
rubrics_metrics.description: FRAM has two distinct sections: FRAM Upload Additional Materials (for file uploads) and Revised Outcome (to type/paste revised text for RPPR section 'I. Outcomes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy guidance appears under the Revised Outcome section and includes a link to samples of acceptable project outcomes. For NIH/Federal awards the Revised Outcome is applicable; SAMHSA awards may not use the Revised Project Outcome section (agency-specific rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM upload mechanics and file handling
rubrics_metrics.description: To upload files: drag and drop or browse; the drop area specifies how many files and what file types are allowed. For uploaded files you can Download (open/download) or Delete the file. Click Delete (bottom of screen) to discard the current FRAM submission package (this does not delete prior submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save the FRAM package before Preview. Preview downloads a PDF summarizing uploaded files, who uploaded, any revised outcome saved, and contents of uploaded files. After submission you cannot change files already submitted, although FRAM Update action remains until Final RPPR acceptance enabling additional uploads.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM revised outcome entry and policy guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a Revised Outcome: read the policy guidance in the Revised Outcome section, then type or paste the revised outcome into the text box; basic formatting tools (bold, italic, bullets, numbering, indent) are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific instructions apply (e.g., SAMHSA). See NIH notices NOT-OD-17-022 and NOT-OD-17-037 for additional guidance and use the samples link on the FRAM screen to view acceptable project outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM submission authority, notifications, and post-submission behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Only SOs or those with delegated authority to submit reports can finalize and submit the FRAM package (Submit button visible only to them). After submission a View action appears on Closeout Status; email notifications are sent to the submitting SO, the PI, and the PO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRAM Update action remains until acceptance of the Final RPPR, enabling more uploads; you cannot modify files already submitted. The PO may rescind approval of the Final RPPR or FPR submission at any time, in which case FRAM Update reappears for submitting FRAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: xTRACT: purpose and submission constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: xTRACT is a module used to create research training tables for inclusion in progress reports and institutional training grant applications; it can pre-populate some data using xTrain and Commons data and allows manual entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: xTRACT is a tool for creating training tables only; tables generated must be attached to and submitted with the appropriate progress report or application. There is no Submit feature in xTRACT. Manually entered information is stored in xTrain and can be reused in later submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: xTrain access and policy pointers
rubrics_metrics.description: xTrain provides online capabilities for working with trainee appointments and termination notices. Roles that can access xTrain include TRAINEE, PI, SO, BO, SPONSOR, and ASST (when delegated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: xTrain has its own online help accessible via help icons or link. Policy references include Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA policy and reporting/assurance requirements for institutions receiving training awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Supplement initiation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Supplements module lets authorized staff initiate an electronic request for additional funds within the scope of the approved project; after initiating you are redirected to ASSIST to complete the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To initiate from eRA Commons you must have a role such as PI, SO, or ASST with Status delegation from the PI. When initiated from eRA Commons, the Parent Grant field is prepopulated and not editable and the Funding Opportunity Announcement number is required. If initiated directly in ASSIST you can initiate without a parent grant number. The eRA option exists even if a NOSI indicates streamlined submissions cannot be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage Administrative Supplement: role-dependent screen behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manage Administrative Supplement screen lets you search for grants to initiate or edit supplements; behavior differs by role: SOs are prompted for search criteria before grants display; PIs have eligible grants automatically displayed; PI delegates have a dropdown to select the PI whose grants to show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an administrative supplement exists, it's listed and the ellipsis menu shows Edit to open it in ASSIST; otherwise Start Application takes you into ASSIST with Parent Grant pre-filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Institution: process overview and required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Change of Institution process lets the current grantee submit a relinquishing statement to Grants Management and allows the receiving organization to access the submitted relinquishing statement; the receiving organization must submit an application via Grants.gov using the Parent FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functionality applies only to NIH grants. Features include creating/viewing/updating/saving/submitting/routing the relinquishing statement via the Commons Status screen, generating a PDF upon submission, and event-generated time-sensitive email notifications to appropriate users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Users and role-specific responsibilities for relinquishing statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Roles involved: Signing Official (SO), Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI), Grants Management Official (GMO) or Grants Management Specialist (GMS). The original organization's SO can start, view, edit, save, route, cancel, delete, and submit the relinquishing statement; receiving organization's SO can view; original PD/PI can view, edit certain fields, and route back to SO; GMO/GMS can view, receive, and return the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PI can edit receiving organization and contact email only if the SO routes the statement to the PD/PI. Routing between SO and PD/PI may occur unlimited times. The SO may submit without PD/PI routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing statement business rules: eligibility and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: All awarded and active grants within their budget period are eligible to be relinquished except those with statuses: 02 – Withdrawn; 21 – Ineligible organization - application withdrawn; 30 – Withdrawn by IC; 34 – Administratively withdrawn by IC prior to review or council. Subprojects, institutional allowances, and supplements are excluded. Relinquishing statements can be submitted for any activity code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Relinquishing Statement search in Status module to find eligible awards (Not Started) to start a new relinquishing statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing statement access, validation, and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At the current award-holding organization any SO can start or submit the relinquishing statement via Status. At the prospective organization, SOs can only access a view-only relinquishing statement. PD/PI routing is not required; SO can submit without routing. Relinquishing statements submitted for pre-award are not validated for the costs relinquished (they can be zero or the original requested amounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system allows multiple relinquishing statement submissions: the SO can submit a new relinquishing statement only if no relinquishing statement has been submitted or if existing statements have been submitted and are now in Accepted for Consideration status. The relinquishing statement can be deleted by the SO only if it is in SO Work In Progress status and has never been submitted. All submitted and accepted versions are visible to the receiving organization. Grant applications for the new organization should be submitted within thirty days after the relinquishing statement is submitted from the former organization, and the relinquishing statement should be submitted within thirty days of the grant application for the new organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing statement search types, statuses, and permissible actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Search types: Not Started (awards eligible to relinquish), Search for Awards (relinquishing statements in-progress at your organization), Search for Relinquishing Statements (awards in process of being relinquished to your organization). Statuses: SO Work in Progress, PD/PI Work in Progress, Submitted to Agency, Accepted for Consideration, Returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available actions depend on status: Start a New Relinquishing Statement (on Not Started results); Edit Relinquishing Statement (while in SO Work in Progress); View Routing History (popup of routing actions and comments); Delete Relinquishing Statement (SO only, SO Work in Progress and never submitted); View Relinquishing Statement (SO can view PDF in Submitted or Accepted; in PD/PI Work in Progress SO sees read-only form). Returned status allows SO to edit and view agency comments via Routing History.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting a new relinquishing statement: organization identification and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: When starting a relinquishing statement identify the receiving organization by typing its name and selecting from suggestions, or by typing its Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) or IPF number. If a valid match is found a Verified symbol appears and fields are populated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you enter a UEI or IPF a Verify button appears which you must click to verify the matching organization. Use Clear and Start Over to clear identifier fields.
